title: From Test Kitchen to Table: A Demo-driven Tour of Foundry Portal for AI Developers | OD836

segments.text: CARLOTTA CASTELLUCCIO: Hi, everyone.
Welcome to this session, From Test Kitchen to Table:
A Demo-Driven Tour of Foundry Portal for AI Developers.
I'm Carlotta Castelluccio.
I'm a Senior AI Advocate at Microsoft,
and I'm here with Nitya.
Hi Nitya.
How are you doing?

So exciting to be at Build again.
Hi everyone.

on the Developer Relations team at Microsoft.

about Microsoft Foundry and specifically about portal.
Where does your journey start?
Every AI development journey has to start
with a business scenario.
In our case, we're going to talk about a retailer called Zava.
Zava is a fictitious enterprise retailer selling home
improvement goods to DIY project enthusiasts.
And you are part of the AI development team.
You are tasked to build Cora, an AI shopping assistant
that can answer customer questions in store or online
and provide customer service.
Now, you want to design Cora to be friendly, helpful,
and cost-effective to deploy.
But you also understand that in this fast-paced environment,
your agent needs to keep adapting to changing conditions,
changing systems, and changing needs.
So what do you do?
Well, let's start first
by understanding what AI app development looks like.
So at a very basic level, an AI app is nothing but a model
that takes an incoming prompt, does some processing on it
and generates a response.
That response can then be used to trigger other actions,
which in turn may generate new prompts and so on
and the cycle continues.
And that's at a very, very basic level.
You can think of this as a monolithic application
where in order for that model to generate that response,
there's other things that happened to coordinate it.
But when we think about scale level delivery,
it becomes more complicated.
Now you have multiple models, multiple prompts,
multiple conversations, and you need to coordinate
and orchestrate all these together.
Plus now you need to extract information
from all these conversations at scale
to determine what you need to do next.
And that is a challenge.
So traditional AI application that's monolithic can't really
do this in a very agile way.
This is where agents can help.
Agent AI brings a microservices-based approach
where every agent is a single unit of work
that can be evolved independently without having
to rewrite the entire system.
What that means is now when you have a giant application,
you can just go in and update or evolve individual agents
without having to think
about how the entire application has to be redeployed.
But to do this, you need a repeatable and simple way.
And what we want to do is talk to you about an analogy.
You need a test kitchen where you can quickly prototype
out these little agents before you put them into production.
And that's the analogy we're using today.
How do you go from test kitchen to table?
Think about your AI application or your AI solution
as the equivalent of a multi-course dinner menu
at a very popular restaurant.
You don't go around designing your recipes right
at the dinner table, rather, test chefs, I mean,
great chefs will have a test kitchen
where they quickly experiment with these recipes
until they get something
that passes their taste test or evaluation.
Then they can take those and move it
into their restaurant kitchen
or code-first development environment to make that better.

test kitchen.
You can go rapidly from a plan to a basic prototype
until your recipe works without writing a single line
of code all in your browser.
So what can Foundry do for you?

of three developer needs that we need.
First, when building these agents
in a microservices approach, we need to rapidly prototype,
build, and deploy them so we can actually have real customers try

Models may change, your prompt requirements may change,
your situation that the environment you are
in may change.
We need ways to do easy experimentation and evaluation
to test these prompts, models, and datasets without having
to reprovision each time.
And last but not least, your app has to be trustworthy.
We need mechanisms for secure, scalable,
and production-ready development.
And that means having a unified end-to-end platform
that provides all these capabilities for us.
So I want to hand off to my colleague to see how we go
about actually building this.
Carlotta.
